 JUDGMENT
This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V. Act 1989 for claiming compensation on account of death of Sri.
Shivakumar B.K., S/o Kempegowda.

2. The brief facts of the case is that, on 30.01.2025 at about 7:00 a.m., within the jurisdiction of Channarayapatna Traffic Police Station, near SCCH - 7 3 MVC No.1298/2025 Mallavanaghatta,
Bangalore - Mangalore NH-75 road, when the deceased Sri. Shivakumar B.K. was riding the unoffending Hero Honda Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 02-V-0501 towards Jogipura, at that time the accused/driver of the offending Truck goods carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-45-0711 following the unoffending vehicle and he drove the same in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result the said the rider/deceased fall in the channel along with the unoffending vehicle & sustained grievous on his legs, head, legs, hands and other parts of the body.

Thereafter the deceased was shifted to Government Hospital, Channarayapatna and thereafter for higher treatment deceased was shifted to Mahalakshmi Manjappa Multi- specialty Hospital, Hassan and thereafter for higher treatment he was shifted to Govt., Hospital, Hassan and at 6.30 p.m. he died due to efficacious of treatment.

sentences.text: Thereafter, Nanje Gowda / Informant lodged complaint before the Channarayapatna Traffic police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.14/2025 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 281 and 106 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023, and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior Officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.

It is contended that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased Shivakumar B.K., and as on the date of the alleged accident the said deceased was aged about 43 years and doing Agriculturist and earning income of Rs.30,000/- p.m.

The petitioners Manjul vs Mohammed Ilyas on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151725886/
2 have claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- under different head of loss of dependency, funeral and obsequies expenses, loss of filial love, loss of consortium and loss of estate etc.,
4.

It is contended that the accident is solely due to the rash or negligent driving of the accused/driver of the offending Truck Goods Carrier bearing Reg. No.KA-45- 0711 and the respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5.
In response to the notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 were appeared through their respective counsels and filed their respective written statements.

6. In the written statement of respondent No.1, he has admitted that he is the owner of the offending vehicle and denied the petition averments in part including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent SCCH - 7 5 MVC No.1298/2025 No.2/Insurance company and any liability, i.e., fastened on him would have to be indemnify by the Respondent No.2 and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

7. In the written statement of respondent No.2, Respondent No.2 the Insurance Company by admitting that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denying the petition averments in part and contended that the Petitioner has not furnished the particulars of the vehicle including the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it is denied having insured the vehicle involved in the accident.
The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL and other documents as per the law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C), 158 of M.V. Act.
Further it is alleged that the alleged accident is occurred due to negligence and fault of the deceased/rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid D.L at the time of alleged accident.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtain the compensation Petitioners have constrained to file the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the deceased and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and SCCH - 7 6 MVC No.1298/2025 reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V.Act.
Hence sought for dismissal of the petition.
8. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.

:: I S S U E S ::
1) Whether the Petitioners proves that on 30.01.2025 at about 7-00 a.m., the deceased was proceeding in unoffending Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-V-501 near Mallavanaghatta, Hassan to Bangalore Road, NH-75 B.M. road Channarayapattana Taluk, Hassan District on the left side of the road, at that time the driver of offending Truck Goods Carrier bearing registration No.KA-45-0711 came from back side in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said Manjul vs Mohammed Ilyas on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151725886/
3 unoffending motor cycle and due to impact the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and during the course of treatment he died?
 2) Whether the Petitioners prove that,
 they are legal heirs of deceased  Shivakumar B.K., S/o  Kempegowda?
3) Whether petitioners are entitled for  compensation?
If so, what is the  quantum?
from whom?
4) What order or award?
In order to prove their claim, the First petitioner is examined herself as PW-1 and got marked the documents Ex.P.1 to 22 and closed their side.

The Superintendent of RTO office Hassan got examined as RW-1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3 and Senior Manager of Insurance Company got examined as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R.4 and Ex.R.5 and closed their side.
10.

I have heard the arguments of both side and perused the written arguments submitted by the respondent no.2.
11.

Having heard the arguments, based on the pleadings and the evidence available on record, I record my findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative Issue No.2 ... In the affirmative Issue No.3 ... Partly in the affirmative Issue No.4...

sentences.text: It is contended that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The respondent No.1 by admitting that he is the owner of the offending vehicle and denied the petition averments and his version is that, the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance company and any liability, i.e.,
fastened on him would have to be SCCH - 7 9 MVC No.1298/2025 indemnify by the Respondent No.2 and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

The Respondent No.2 admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle, however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
Further it is alleged that, driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid D.L, at the time of alleged accident.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtain the compensation Petitioners have constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age,
income and occupation of the deceased and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the petition.
14.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioners.

Hence, in order to prove their case,
the Petitioner No.1 herself examined as P.W.1 and she has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in her evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to Ex.P.22 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.
Ex.P-1 is the FIR in Cr.No.14/2025 of Channarayapatna Traffic P.S.

Ex.P.2 is SCCH - 7 10 MVC No.1298/2025 the Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Police intimation copy, Ex.P.4 is the further complaint copy, Ex.P.5 is the Charge sheet alteration requisition, Ex.P.6 is the Spot mahazar, Ex.P.7 is the Spot Sketch, Ex.P.8 is the Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P9 is the notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P10 is the Statement of Complainant witness, eye witness and PW.1.
Ex. P11

Out patient record / MLC, Ex.P12 is the Inquest, Ex.P13 is the P.M. report, Ex.P14 is the Charge sheet, Ex.P15 is the Discharge summary, Ex.P16 is the 19 Medical bills for Rs.6,481/-, Ex.P17 to 20 Notarized copies of Aadhar cards of deceased and Petitioners, Ex.P21 is the Notarized copy of D.L. of deceased and Ex.P22 is the Notarized copy of death certificate of deceased.

15. In the cross-examination of PW-1 by the counsel for Respondent No.2 she has deposed that her brother-in- law Nanjegowda has lodged the complaint and he is an eye witness to the alleged incident and at the time of alleged accident he was riding the two wheeler by following the unoffending vehicle.
She don't know the distance between the said vehicles.

At the time of alleged accident the driver of the offending vehicle has dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending Manjul vs Mohammed Ilyas on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151725886/
5 vehicle and caused the alleged accident, as a result the said unoffending vehicle was damaged and the deceased has sustained grievous injuries.
The rider of the unoffending vehicle is her husband and he is the RC owner of the said SCCH - 7 11 MVC No.1298/2025 vehicle.
Further she has denied that, the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle is not damaged.

Further she has denied that, at the time of alleged accident the rider of the unoffending vehicle rode the same in a high speed and in negligent manner and due to his fault dashed head on collusion against the offending vehicle.
Further she has denied that at the time of alleged accident, the deceased was not wear the helmet and he is riding the said vehicle in the wrong way.
Further, she has deposed that after the alleged accident, the deceased was shifted to Channarayapatna Govt., hospital.
Further she has deposed that, she has not incurred Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical expenditure.
She has not produced documents to show that, the deceased was earning income of Rs.30,000/- from the Agriculture.
Further she has denied that, at the time of alleged accident the deceased was aged about 46 years.
Further she has denied that the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the deceased and no fault of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further she has denied that in order to get the compensation, in collusion with the police they have filed the false case against the driver of the offending vehicle and falsely implicated the offending vehicle and produced concocted and created documents and deposing falsely.
During the cross examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition and she has made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

In order to prove the version of Respondent No.2, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Senior Manager as RW-2 and he has reiterated the entire version averments and contentions taken in the course of written statement in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.R.4 and Ex.R.5 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the RW-2.
Ex.R.4 is the copy of Authorization letter and Ex.R.5 is the Insurance Policy.
17. In the cross-examination of RW-2 by Petitioner's counsel he has deposed that he is deposing on the basis of the police documents.
After investigation the police have filed Charge Sheet against the Accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
The said Charge Sheet is not challenged before the Higher authority or competent court.
The driver of the offending vehicle is possessing D.L. to drive the L.M.V. Vehicles.

The insurance policy of the offending vehicle is in force, as per its terms and conditions and the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid driving licence to drive the offending vehicle at the time of alleged accident.

During the investigation, the police have not properly verified the D.L. of the accused and therefore, they have not filed charge sheet against the accused in relating to not possessing valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of alleged accident.
Further he has denied that the SCCH - 7 13 MVC No.1298/2025 alleged accident occurred due to fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further he has denied that in order to escape from his liability he has filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.
18. The Respondent No.2 got examined RTO of Hassan as RW-1 and he has produced Ex.R.1 to 3 documents.
Ex.R1 is the Authorization letter, Ex.R2 is the true copy of B register extract of offending vehicle and Ex.R3 is the true copy of D.L. extract of accused.

In the examination in chief he has Manjul vs Mohammed Ilyas on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151725886/
6 deposed that, the gross laden weight of the offending vehicle is 9600 kgs.

The accused / driver of the offending vehicle has possessing D.L. to drive the Motor cycle with gear and LMV vehicles and vehicles of less than gross laden weight of 7500 kg and that D.L. is valid for a period from 15.10.2020 to 11.12.2041.
The accused / driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing driving licence to drive the offending vehicle.
In the cross examination of RW.1 by counsel for Petitioner he has deposed that, the driver of the offending vehicle has possessing the D.L. to drive the LMV vehicles upto laden weight of 7500 kg.
Further he has denied that, the driver of the offending vehicle is possessing valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of alleged accident.

19. On careful reading of Ex.P8/IMV report, it specifies that the Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said incident was not occurred due to any SCCH - 7 14 MVC No.1298/2025 mechanical defects of the motor vehicles and further the said inspector noticed the damages to the offending vehicle that, Front left side corner of the body dented, inwards left side head light assembly damaged.
Front left side bumper damaged, Front left side indicator assembly damaged.

Further the said inspector noticed the damages to the unoffending vehicle that, front crush guard pressed inwards, head light assembly full damaged, head light mark damaged, T handle damaged,
meter assembly damaged, both side indicators broken both side mirror broken tail lamp assembly damaged, rear wheel mud guard damaged, rear indicators damaged, read wheel both side suspension damaged.
20.
On going through the Ex.P-13/Postmortem report it is seen that Doctor opined that cause of death of deceased is due to multiple injuries sustained and their Sequelae.

21. On going through the Ex.P-2/Complaint and Ex.P4 further complaint, it is seen that on 30.01.2025 at about 7:00 a.m., near Mallavanaghatta, on Bangalore - Mangalore NH-75 road, when the deceased Sri. Shivakumar B.K. was riding the unoffending Hero Honda Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-V-0501 towards Jogipura, at that time the accused/driver of the offending Truck goods carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-45-0711 following the unoffending vehicle and he drove the same in a high SCCH - 7 15 MVC No.1298/2025 speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result the said the rider/deceased fall in the channel along with the unoffending vehicle & sustained grievous on his legs, head, legs, hands and other parts of the body. Thereafter the deceased was shifted to Government Hospital,
Channarayapatna and thereafter for higher treatment deceased was shifted to Mahalakshmi Manjappa Multi-specialty Hospital, Hassan and thereafter for higher treatment he was shifted to Govt., Hospital, Hassan and at 6.30 p.m. he died due to efficacious of treatment.
The alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
22. Admittedly, the accused is the driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that deceased Shivakumar B.K. died due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

The counsel for Respondents were claimed the said Accused to be innocent and further they have contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the deceased and no fault of the accused and the said offending vehicle is falsely implicated in this case and the said vehicle is no nexus to the alleged accident.

On going through the prosecution papers i.e, FIR, Complaint, Police intimation, Further complaint, Spot mahazar, Spot Sketch, MVA Report, Inquest, Postmortem Manjul vs Mohammed Ilyas on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151725886/
7 report and Charge Sheet SCCH - 7 16 MVC No.1298/2025 and the evidence of PW-1 are specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/Complaint, Ex.P3 further complaint and Ex.P14 - Charge Sheet.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and at the spot dashed against the unoffending vehicle,
as a result the deceased Shivakumar B.K. sustained grievous injury and died due to alleged accident.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P.2/Complaint, Ex.P4/further complaint, Ex.P6/Spot mahazar, Ex.P7/spot sketch, Ex.P-8/MVA report, Ex.P12/Inquest, Ex.P-13/Postmortem Report and Ex.P- 14/Charge Sheet clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.

It is not in dispute as to SCCH - 7 17 MVC No.1298/2025 the aspect that, the deceased Shivakumar B.K.
sustained grievous injuries and died in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively, it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Sri. Shivakumar B.K. noted in the Ex.P13/PM report would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 106 & 281 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the death of the innocent man/Shivakumar B.K. aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
23. Issue No.2 and 3:-
The Learned counsel for the Petitioners has contended that the deceased was aged about 43 years and doing Agriculture work and earning income of Rs.30,000/- p.m.

Further the counsel contended that as per the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General SCCH - 7 18 MVC No.1298/2025 Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, the Petitioners being legal heirs of deceased, each of the Petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of love and affection consortium and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.
24.

sentences.text: On the other hand the learned counsel for Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioners claimed that the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., the same is not established by the claimants by producing the documents.
Since the Petitioners have not established the income of the deceased, they are not entitled for compensation towards future prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.

Manjul vs Mohammed Ilyas on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151725886/
8 25.
On going through the Ex.P-17 to Ex.P.20/Adhar Cards it is seen that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased.
Hence on the strength of Ex.P-17 to Ex.P.20 it is crystal clear that the Petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.

26. The petitioners have contended that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 43 years and they relied on the Ex.P.21/D.L. Card of the deceased and wherein the date of birth of the deceased is shown as SCCH - 7 19 MVC No.1298/2025 01.06.1980 and this accident was took place on 30.01.2025.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 44 years, 7 months and 29 days.
Therefore, the age of the deceased is considered as 44 years at the time of accident.
27. It is not in dispute that the deceased died in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
In the instance case the petitioners claimed that deceased was doing Agriculture work and earning income of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
But they have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2025, the notional income of the deceased taken at Rs.16,250/-.
28.

To the aforesaid income, 25% to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the constitution bench of the Supreme Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157 in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethy and other.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus the monthly income comes to Rs.20,312/-
(Rs.16,250/- + 25%).

Since the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased, hence it is appropriate to deduct 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses and SCCH - 7 20 MVC No.1298/2025 remaining amount, i.e., Rs.13,542/- (Rs.20,312/- - Rs.6,770/-) has to be taken as his/deceased contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 44 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '14'.
Thus the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.22,75,056/- (Rs.13,542/- x 12 x 14) on account of loss of dependency.
29. In addition to that, the Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Loss of estate and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Funeral expenses.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2018 ACJ 2782 in the Case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram, Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioners No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of loss of filial consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- each under the head of love and affection.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the Pranay Sethi's case the Hon'ble Apex court in the year 2016 has stated that it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards consortium for dependents and this sum was to be increased by 10% every three years and consequently as of 2025, a sum of Rs.51,997/- is to be paid to each of the dependents towards head of loss of filial consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses caused by the loss of a deceased.

It SCCH - 7 21 MVC No.1298/2025 cannot be in dispute that the loss of a deceased causes a devastating blow to the dependents and the degree of pain and agony would be at its speak and would linger forever it is for this reason an adequate sum is required to be awarded.
This sum can also be increased every year by adducing the record date of the inflation henceforth.

Accordingly now coming to the matter on hand, the Petitioners are entitled Manjul vs Mohammed Ilyas on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151725886/
9 to compensation of Rs.19,500/- on account of Loss of estate and compensation of Rs.19,500/- on account of Funeral expenses.

The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioners No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.51,997/- each under the head of loss of consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- each under the head of love and affection.
30. Further the Petitioners have produced hospital and medical bills, towards medical expenses as per Ex.P.16 for an amount of Rs.66,481/-.
Hence the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.66,481/- under the head of hospital and medical expenses.

Thus the Petitioners are entitled to the following compensation:
31.

The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:

Medical expenses 66,481-00 Total 26,86,528-00 32.

The Petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.26,86,528/-.
33.

The Respondent No.2/Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and alleged that the driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid and effective D.L to drive the offending vehicle at the time of alleged accident and accordingly there is violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.

34. In the instance case it is admitted fact that, the driver of the offending vehicle has pursued DL to drive the LMV and MCWG vehicles and in the instant case the offending vehicle is MGV Goods Carrier, as such, the driver of the offending vehicle has not possessing valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending vehicle at the time of the alleged accident and therefore there is clear violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, as such in view of breach of the policy condition the Petitioner prays to direct the Insurance Company to pay the compensation and recover from the SCCH - 7 23 MVC No.1298/2025 owner/ Respondent No.1 of the offending vehicle.

The principle of pay and recovery is explained in detail in the decision reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208 in the case of Pappu and Others V/s Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another and (2018) 9 SCC 650 in the case of Shamanna and another V/s Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., and others and the Hon'ble Court held that the award passed against insured owner to be paid by the insurer and recovered from owner.

sentences.text: ....It is crystal clear that the object of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, either before the amendment or thereafter, particularly covered by Chapter XI thereof, is to compensate victims of accidents in case of an insurance policy being in existence.

In view of the interpretation made, holding that omission of the proviso would exonerate the insurer of its liability to indemnify at the first instance would be too wild a proposition and would result in creating a situation where the insurer would be out of scene despite an insurance policy being there and the claimants would have to again fight for getting the amount SCCH - 7 27 MVC No.1298/2025 of compensation through execution proceedings in one way or the other, searching the owner through the process of Court.

In such an event, the claimants would face further harassment and nobody knows that despite a money decree in the nature of an award being there in their favour, as to whether the claimants would ever be able to get the compensation realized through recovery proceedings directly from the owner.
Accordingly, the legislative intent becomes clear and there is nothing to support the insurer's arguments flowing from interpretation of Statute or Causus Omissus.
The contention advanced on behalf of insurer stands discarded.

Thus the lordship concluded that:
38.

The Court, therefore, holds that mere omission of proviso attached to sub- section (4) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 after its replacement by Section 150 of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (32 of 2019), neither takes away the liability of the insurer to pay the claimants nor its right to recover the said amount from the owner.

The law to this effect remains intact and unaffected by Amendment Act, 2019 and, hence, insurer shall continue to indemnify the owner's risk in relation to accidents taking place after 01.04.2022 and "PAY & RECOVER"
principle will still continue to govern the field advancing social object of the Statute protecting third party interest.

Principle of law laid down by the Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Swaran Singh and others, JT 2004 (1) SC 109 has not lost SCCH - 7 28 MVC No.1298/2025 its significance and binding effect despite omission of proviso.

3) Whether petitioners are entitled for  compensation?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and at the spot dashed against the unoffending vehicle,
as a result the deceased Shivakumar B.K. sustained grievous injury and died due to alleged accident.
It is not in dispute as to SCCH - 7 17 MVC No.1298/2025 the aspect that, the deceased Shivakumar B.K.
sustained grievous injuries and died in the alleged incident.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Sri. Shivakumar B.K. noted in the Ex.P13/PM report would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 106 & 281 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the death of the innocent man/Shivakumar B.K. aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
On going through the Ex.P-17 to Ex.P.20/Adhar Cards it is seen that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased.
Hence on the strength of Ex.P-17 to Ex.P.20 it is crystal clear that the Petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
But they have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2025, the notional income of the deceased taken at Rs.16,250/-.
28.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2018 ACJ 2782 in the Case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram, Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioners No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of loss of filial consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- each under the head of love and affection.
The principle of pay and recovery is explained in detail in the decision reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208 in the case of Pappu and Others V/s Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another and (2018) 9 SCC 650 in the case of Shamanna and another V/s Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., and others and the Hon'ble Court held that the award passed against insured owner to be paid by the insurer and recovered from owner.
Principle of law laid down by the Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Swaran Singh and others, JT 2004 (1) SC 109 has not lost SCCH - 7 28 MVC No.1298/2025 its significance and binding effect despite omission of proviso.
Hence in view of the position of law in the above recent decisions, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the award amount and Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle shall pay the compensation to the Petitioners and the Respondent No.2 Insurance Company shall recover the same from the Respondent No.1/owner of the offending vehicle.
